user.description: Choose the Truma appliance to add. It must already be paired with this Home Assistant host — see the documentation.

confirm.description:
Do you want to set up {name}?

The appliance only accepts a host it has been paired with. If it has not been paired yet, do that first — the documentation describes how.

abort.no_devices_found: No Truma appliance found in range. Make sure it is powered and within reach of a connectable Bluetooth adapter.
abort.not_reachable: The appliance was in range a moment ago but is not now. It changes its Bluetooth address constantly, so try again.

error.cannot_pair: Could not pair with the appliance. It only accepts new clients while it is in its pairing state and has a free client slot — start pairing on the unit, or remove a device you no longer use in the Truma app, then try again.

no_bluetooth_proxy.title: Truma Aventa needs a Bluetooth proxy
no_bluetooth_proxy.description:
{address} can only be reached through this host's own Bluetooth adapter.

The appliance changes its Bluetooth address between connections and only accepts a reconnect from a client that can resolve that address back to the pairing. Home Assistant's host adapter cannot do this, so the connection will keep dropping no matter how good the signal is.

An ESPHome Bluetooth proxy built on the esp-idf framework resolves the address the way a phone does. Place one within a few metres of the appliance. The documentation has a ready-made configuration.
